newsitem.title: USA: Tighter Brent market aids U.S. crude grade uptick.
newsitem.headline: Tighter Brent market aids U.S. crude grade uptick.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes climbed higher Friday on a technical spurt for outright values, while domestic grade barrels found stronger differentials on a tighter North Sea Brent market, traders said.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended the week around 10 cents firmer at $20.35-45 a barrel, turning a contango market to backwardation on bullish prompt month fundamentals.

Contango markets are a bearish indicator, allowing the second month to hold premiums to the front. Friday saw the June/July roll hover around plus 4-6 cents most of the session, and talk late around 2-3 cents in June's favor.
Grade players said deals stagnated at firmer differentials established in the morning, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James safely set at a 6-8 cents advantage to the benchmark.
Deals were seen for LLS at 7-8 cents over WTI. Cash players said the advances were mostly tied to Brent.
"We came higher on tighter Brent markets, the Brent spreads moving into backwardation and tighter Dated Brent," said a Texas cash trader.
Midland/WTI sold at discounts of 30 and 31 cents to the June WTI/Cushing, steady from Thursday. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire sold at WTI minus 32 cents, a shade firmer than yesterday's deals.
For the sours, West Texas Sour/Midland moved at discounts of $1.47, $1.49 and $1.50 to the marker, steady from Thursday.
June WTI/Cushing Postings Plus business was one of the session's features, with deals done between $2.00-07 in an actively traded market.
P-Plus values were some 10 cents firmer than yesterday, and came on the revolving movement of June/July spreads.
